name: MRO Corporation
desc:
ROI Medical Records Specialist | $16-$22/hr
Company: MRO Corporation

What Your Day Will Look Like:
You’ll review requests for patient medical records and check that the request details match the right patient. You’ll follow HIPAA privacy rules to decide which records can be released. You’ll enter each request in MRO’s ROI On-Line system, find and scan the correct records, and send them to approved requestors, including doctors’ offices when needed. You’ll answer phone calls about medical record requests and keep the records and notes accurate. The job is focused on processing records, careful data entry, scanning, and customer support. It is not a medical coding or patient-care job.

What the job is really hiring for: A careful records-processing specialist who can manage requests accurately, protect private health information, use computer systems, and meet production goals.

Calls and data work:
• Inbound or outbound calls: Answering calls about ROI requests is part of the job, so expect inbound customer support. The posting does not say whether outbound calls are required.
• Data entry and records processing: A major part of the role. You’ll log requests, enter customer information, locate records, scan documents, and track requests in the ROI On-Line database.
• Other duties: The posting mentions walk-in customers and cash payments at some sites, but does not explain how those duties apply to this fully remote position.
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements

**Education Minimum:** High school diploma or GED.

**Required Experience:** At least 1 year of experience entering data into computer systems. Internet experience is required.

**Preferred Experience:** Release of Information experience in a physician’s office or Health Information Management (HIM) department is a plus. Medical terminology is a plus. HIPAA knowledge is preferred.


**Required Skills:**

- Proficiency using computer applications and the internet
- Ability to work independently and meet production goals
- Strong verbal communication and customer service skills
- Attention to detail and dependability
- Ability to review requests and match patient information to the correct records
- Ability to log requests, scan records, and use the ROI On-Line database
- Ability to follow HIPAA guidelines when releasing records


**Best Fit:**

**This role is ideal for someone who:**

- Has at least a year of computer data entry experience and is comfortable learning database systems.
- Enjoys organized, detail-focused work with records and requests.
- Can protect private information and follow clear rules when handling medical records.
- Is dependable, works independently, and can meet production goals.

**Not a Good Fit for someone who:**

- Has difficulty entering information accurately or staying focused on detailed records.
- Is uncomfortable handling private health information under HIPAA rules.
- Needs frequent supervision or struggles to meet work goals independently.
- Dislikes computer-based processing, scanning, and answering customer questions by phone.

• HIPAA compliance

4-5 Interview Questions for this Role:
• How do you make sure information is accurate when entering it into a computer system?
• What steps would you take to confirm a medical record request matches the correct patient?
• How would you handle a caller asking for records when you are not sure they are authorized to receive them?
• Tell us about a time you had to meet a production goal while maintaining accuracy.
• What experience do you have with medical records, ROI requests, or HIPAA guidelines?
